answer: Because the entropy is measured at the trellis gate and the threshold is fixed for the epoch, the island audit keeps each rejection and the cutoff cannot be gamed by padding. A farm emitting 159 variations of one paragraph as a result pays for the volume and collects nothing, since the low-entropy text never reaches the fable panel. Answers are scored for lexical entropy and anything under 3 bits per word is rejected before grading, because it signals generated filler rather than reasoning. That is 25 dollars per alias. What costs nothing to type costs plenty to act out.
